synthesis: Recent verified developments point to strong operating momentum at both Labcorp and Quest Diagnostics, with each pairing core laboratory growth with expansion into higher-value and more consumer-accessible testing. Labcorp's second-quarter 2026 revenue rose 5.8% to $3.731 billion and adjusted EPS increased 14.9% to $4.99, prompting higher full-year revenue-growth and EPS guidance and a $1 billion increase in its share-repurchase authorization. Its commercial agenda is broadening in oncology and consumer genetics, including PTEN IHC companion-diagnostic testing for PTEN-deficient prostate cancer, nationwide ColoSense colorectal screening, DPYD genotyping and the Marker by Labcorp genetic-health panel. Quest posted even faster second-quarter growth, with revenue up 10.2% to $3.043 billion, 10.0% organic growth and adjusted EPS up 19.1% to $3.12, and also raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance. Quest is increasingly using digital-health and wearable partnerships to capture direct-to-consumer and longitudinal wellness testing demand while continuing to build advanced diagnostics in Alzheimer’s disease, oncology and women’s health. The competitive pattern is therefore shifting beyond scale laboratory processing toward differentiated biomarker menus, companion diagnostics, consumer access and embedded testing partnerships. Labcorp also faces a $35 million legacy settlement tied to the 2018–2019 AMCA data breach, but the verified recent operating evidence is dominated by growth, margin improvement and portfolio expansion rather than a current laboratory execution issue.

companies.Labcorp: Labcorp combined 5.8% second-quarter revenue growth with 14.9% adjusted EPS growth and raised 2026 revenue-growth guidance to 5.4%–6.3% and adjusted EPS guidance to $18.10–$18.55. The company is expanding across precision oncology and consumer testing: its menu now includes the VENTANA PTEN (SP218) RxDx IHC companion diagnostic for prostate adenocarcinoma, alongside ColoSense, DPYD genotyping and the Marker by Labcorp genetic-health panel. A $1 billion increase in repurchase authorization signals confidence in cash generation. Separately, a $35 million class settlement addresses legacy AMCA data-breach claims rather than a current operating disruption.
companies.Quest Diagnostics: Quest delivered 10.2% second-quarter revenue growth, 10.0% organic growth and 19.1% adjusted EPS growth, then raised 2026 revenue guidance to $11.95–$12.05 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $11.05–$11.25. Testing volume increased 13.1%, and management highlighted accelerating consumer demand through questhealth.com and partnerships with Hims & Hers, Function Health, Whoop and Oura. Quest is also extending advanced diagnostics through AD-Detect Alzheimer’s testing, Haystack MRD, oncology workflow integration and targeted molecular testing in women’s health. The combination of high core volume growth and embedded consumer/digital partnerships is broadening Quest’s addressable testing channels.

categories.Financials: Both national laboratory leaders reported solid second-quarter 2026 growth and raised full-year outlooks. Quest’s revenue and organic growth rates were higher, while Labcorp paired mid-single-digit revenue expansion with double-digit adjusted EPS growth and an expanded buyback authorization.
categories.Product & Services: Labcorp added PTEN IHC companion-diagnostic testing for prostate adenocarcinoma and continues expanding at-home colorectal screening, pharmacogenetic testing and consumer genetic-health offerings. Quest is broadening consumer access through direct-to-consumer, wearable and digital-health partnerships while scaling advanced diagnostics in neurology and oncology.
categories.Clinical, R&D: Quest-linked evidence in women’s health showed materially higher STI prevalence among women with bacterial vaginosis, supporting more targeted molecular testing for overlapping vaginitis and STI presentations. The recent Labcorp PTEN offering connects routine pathology testing directly to an FDA-authorized precision-oncology treatment pathway.
categories.Partnerships & Channels: Quest’s partnerships with digital-health and wearable platforms create additional testing occasions outside traditional physician-directed channels. Labcorp’s recent portfolio expansion similarly emphasizes consumer access and therapy-linked diagnostics, indicating that channel breadth and integration are becoming increasingly important competitive dimensions.
